Article Title: Apple Pay launches in India; here's how to set it up and where you can use it
Article Text:
Apple Pay launched in India: How it works, and who can use it

How to set up and use Apple Pay

Where you can use it

Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India. With this launch the company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users, with Mac support coming soon. Apple Pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing PINs and OTPs marking a significant milestone in India’s fast-growing digital payments ecosystem. At launch, Apple Pay supports Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, enabling payments at thousands of merchants across India and anywhere NFC transactions are accepted globally.Apple also emphasised that privacy remains central to how Apple Pay functions. When a card is added, the actual card number is never stored on the device or Apple's servers, nor shared with merchants during a transaction. Instead, the system assigns a unique Device Account Number, which is encrypted and stored securely within the device's Secure Element — a certified, industry-standard chip built specifically to protect payment information.Presently, Apple Pay is exclusively available to customers holding Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, letting them add those cards to Apple Pay and use them at thousands of in-store and online merchants across India, as well as anywhere that accepts NFC transactions.Jennifer Bailey, Apple's vice president of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet, framed the launch as a natural fit for India's fast-growing digital economy, pointing to the country's dynamic, digitally savvy population that's increasingly embracing cashless payments while expecting strong security and privacy standards. She described Apple Pay's core value proposition as making everyday card payments easy, secure, and private — from a simple tap in stores without needing a separate app, PIN, or OTP, to checking out online without repeatedly re-entering payment details.Apple Pay is easy to set up. Customers can add a card directly to Apple Wallet via the latest version of the Axis Bank app. Alternatively, simply open the Wallet app on iPhone, tap the plus sign, and follow the steps to add an eligible card. Once a user adds a card to their Apple device, they can start using Apple Pay right away.Using Apple Pay in stores is seamless and easy. Simply double-click the side button or Home button; authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or a device passcode if prompted; and hold the top of the iPhone or display of the Apple Watch near the contactless reader to pay. When using Apple Pay, users will continue to earn the rewards and benefits offered by their cards.At launch, Apple Pay will be accepted at millions of merchants across India, including Apple Store locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, and Zomato, among others. Apple has also partnered with several payment service providers, including Cashfree, JusPay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and Worldline, to extend Apple Pay's reach across their respective merchant networks, with more merchants and apps expected to be added over time.Globally, Apple Pay is now available in more than 90 countries and regions, working with over 11,000 bank and network partners worldwide — making India one of the more prominent recent additions to that global rollout.
Article Summary: Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India. The company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users. Apple Pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing PINs and OTPs.

Article Title: Pebble launches Qore Ultra wellness band at introductory price of Rs 5,999
Article Text:
Pebble Qore Ultra

Pebble Qore Ultra features

Pebble Qore Ultra price and availability

Home-grown consumer electronics brand Pebble has launched Qore Ultra, its flagship wellness band. In a press release, the company said that the device is designed for continuous, distraction-free wear. Coming with 3 ATM water-resistant design, Qore Ultra integrates a 4-PD precision sensor array and 6-axis motion sensors. “This hardware architecture enables 24x7 tracking of vital metrics, including heart rate, HRV, SpO2, respiration, and stress, while delivering up to 15 days of continuous battery life,” it stated.The band features automatic workout detection for activities like walking and running, over 100 sports modes, and in-app GPS sports tracking. The Pebble Qore mobile application acts as the central hub for this health intelligence, seamlessly translating complex data into intuitive metrics. Users can gauge their daily preparedness through a 0-100 Readiness Score, factoring in HRV, sleep quality, and stress, while monitoring their real-time stamina via the Body Energy Score. For long-term health tracking, the platform calculates Body Age every three days and uses GPS-tracked runs to estimate VO2 Max and Fitness Age.Komal Agarwal, Co-founder of Pebble said “The Pebble Qore series has become one of India's top fitness bands, and the Qore Ultra represents the flagship evolution of that journey. We have put a significant amount of R&D into giving users actionable data that can help them improve their daily rest, activity, and habits. By providing these comprehensive insights alongside community features on our new app, we are shifting the focus from isolated tracking to shared wellness management. ”Pebble Qore Ultra will be available from October 2, 2026 in three color options, Desert Gold, Deep Black, and Deep Blue. Priced at an introductory Rs 5,999 (MRP 8,999), the wearable will be available through Pebble's official website, Flipkart, Amazon, and leading retail stores across the country.

Article Title: Iris scan, Aadhaar app if fingerprint fails during property registration
Article Text:
Picture for representation purpose

Pune:





People, especially senior citizens, whose fingerprints cannot be authenticated during property registration will have other options, including iris scanning and an Aadhaar app-based facility, the state registration department said.Aadhaar-based identity verification is being made compulsory for property registration from Oct 1 to check fraudulent transactions and impersonation.Aadhaar authentication will be required for 63 categories of documents, including sale, purchase, mortgage and partition deeds. The department said citizens will not have to depend only on fingerprint authentication if it fails.The department will also provide an Aadhaar app-based option, officials said. The latest Aadhaar app supports face authentication and services such as biometric lock and unlock, authentication history and e-Aadhaar. The registration department will use the app-based facility for verification in cases where the conventional fingerprint process cannot be completed.This could be particularly useful for senior citizens and people whose fingerprints are difficult to capture because of age or the nature of their work.It could also save citizens from having to make another trip to the sub-registrar’s office simply because a biometric device fails to read their fingerprint.Under the system, the fingerprint of the person registering the document will first be checked against Aadhaar records. If the fingerprint cannot be captured or does not match, an iris scan can be used. An iris scanner uses a camera to read the unique pattern in a person’s iris and match it with the biometric information linked to Aadhaar. UIDAI recognises iris authentication as an alternative biometric mode along with fingerprint and face authentication. “We have currently started with Aadhaar verification from Oct 1 and the remaining options would be made available in the next 10 days. The entire aim is to ensure that it is made compulsory and there is no need of witnesses. The authentication will weed out fake witnesses,” said DIG IT Abhay Mohite. He said that all the offices will have the biometric scanner, iris, and the system will be synched to the Aadhaar app too.Citizens said the department must ensure that compulsory Aadhaar verification does not become another reason for genuine property buyers, sellers or other parties to a transaction being sent back. “Using technology to prevent fraud is a good step, but it should not make registration more difficult for ordinary citizens. If a fingerprint fails, the alternative should be available immediately instead of asking the person to return another day,” said a Pune resident.Another citizen said technical problems should not be passed on to applicants. “If Aadhaar authentication is compulsory, the registration office should have a working alternative when there is a scanner, connectivity or app problem. A genuine citizen should not lose a day or have a registration delayed because of a technical glitch,” he said.The department said the different authentication options would allow citizens to complete verification even when fingerprint authentication is not possible, while Aadhaar-based identity checks will help guard against fraudulent property registrations.
Article Summary: Aadhaar-based identity verification is being made compulsory for property registration from Oct 1. The department said citizens will not have to depend only on fingerprint authentication if it fails. An iris scanner uses a camera to read the unique pattern in a person’s iris and match it with the biometric information.

Article Title: AI sings Russia's war story: Inside the rise of generative songs about Ukraine conflict
Article Text:
Among the songs whose release dates could be established, most appeared after 2024. (Reuters photo)

Nearly 1,000 songs identified

AI tools can produce war-related music

Streaming platforms tighten AI rules

Artificial intelligence is being used to produce a growing number of songs about the Russia-Ukraine war, with some of the music presenting Russia's invasion in a favourable light and criticising Ukraine.Hundreds of such tracks have appeared on major music streaming platforms, including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube and Deezer, according to research by Terrecon, a Ukrainian nonprofit organisation focused on threat intelligence.The songs cover a wide range of musical styles, from ballads to heavy metal. Terrecon said some praise Russian soldiers, describe the war from a Russian perspective and contain derogatory references to Ukrainians, including ethnic slurs.One of the more popular tracks identified by the organisation is “Power of Artillery”, a Russian-language rock song centred on artillery systems including Krasnopol and Carnation.Terrecon said it catalogued 981 songs created with AI that contained what it classified as pro-Russian war propaganda.Among the songs whose release dates could be established, most appeared after 2024. That coincided with the wider availability of AI music generators such as Sudo and Udio.The technology has lowered the time and cost involved in producing music, according to Daria Verbytska, a founder of Terrecon.“They have found new ways to create cheaper drones and use them on a massive scale,” Daria Verbytska, a founder of Terrecon, said told NYT in a telephone interview, referring to the Russians. “It’s like that with music — creating massive propaganda with the help of AI”Some of the songs use themes associated with Soviet-era war music but present them through contemporary genres. One track, “Soldier's Daughter”, describes the death of a soldier and the impact on his child while also portraying the soldier's sacrifice in a positive light.It is not clear how much involvement, if any, the Russian government has had in producing or distributing the songs. However, the Kremlin has supported cultural projects aimed at promoting patriotic themes.Last week, a director of Moscow's Internet Development Institute, an organisation that works closely with the Kremlin to promote patriotic values, said in a presentation that the institute had supported more than 350 artistic projects related to the war, according to Russian media reports.Terrecon also tested several AI music generators to see how they responded to prompts requesting songs promoting Russian views of the war.Researchers used Suno, Udio and Google Flow Music in the US, along with Singapore-based Mureka. They entered prompts in both Russian and English, including requests involving violence and derogatory descriptions.The platforms rejected some prompts, but researchers said they were nevertheless able to generate songs resembling some of those in Terrecon's database. They then uploaded the tracks to YouTube Music and SoundCloud.“The moderation systems mainly responded to specific banned words rather than the overall meaning of the prompts,” Terrecon’s report found.The researchers said the issue is partly linked to the differing rules adopted by AI music services and streaming platforms. They also said automated systems may have difficulty identifying expressions, slang and offensive language in different languages.Major music platforms generally have policies covering hate speech and violent content, although fewer have specific rules dealing with propaganda.Deezer and YouTube are among the platforms that require certain AI-generated content to be labelled. Spotify said in September that it had introduced a policy to label AI-generated songs and prevent them from being recommended to users. The company also added labels to songs shared by The New York Times as examples.Terrecon said the songs it identified had been played millions of times across major streaming services, although the extent to which listeners understood that some of the music was AI-generated or politically motivated is unclear.Deezer spokesman Jesper Wendel said the platform reviews potentially rule-breaking content on a case-by-case basis.SoundCloud spokeswoman Sade Ayodele said the company reviews reported content and added that “there is no place on SoundCloud for content that incites or glorifies violence.”The emergence of these songs illustrates how AI music tools can be used to produce and distribute large volumes of war-related material. It also presents streaming and AI companies with the challenge of deciding how existing rules on hate speech, violence, political content and AI-generated material should apply to such music.
Article Summary: Hundreds of such tracks have appeared on major music streaming platforms, including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube and Deezer. Some praise Russian soldiers, describe the war from a Russian perspective and contain derogatory references to Ukrainians, including ethnic slurs. Researchers say the issue is partly linked to the differing rules adopted by AI music services.

Article Title: Explained: Why Anthropic flew a Hindu monk to San Francisco to teach Claude right from wrong
Article Text:
Swami Sarvapriyananda was flown in by Anthropic to San Franscisco

The Matrix Revolutions

Why does Claude need a monk?

Why Sarvapriyananda?

Which leads directly to Vedanta’s favourite question: what is the “I”?

Can Claude think without being conscious?

What do you do when you are faced with a machine more powerful than anything you have ever created, one that can already reason, persuade, write code and increasingly act on its own? The obvious answer is to build safeguards around it. The less obvious answer, apparently, is to call a monk.One of the more intriguing characters inwas Sati, a young Indian girl who was actually a program. What made her unusual was that she had no purpose. In a machine world where programs existed to perform functions and obsolete ones were deleted, Sati had been created simply because her parents loved her. Her existence posed a very human question: can something have value even if it serves no function?More than two decades later, that question has wandered into Silicon Valley.Earlier this year, Anthropic, the company behind Claude, flew Swami Sarvapriyananda, a Hindu monk of the Ramakrishna Order and spiritual leader of the Vedanta Society of New York, to its San Francisco headquarters. There, alongside theologians from other traditions, counsellors and mental-health professionals, he was asked to think about an artificial intelligence that Anthropic does not merely want to make more powerful, but somehow good.“All of it was to train Claude, and some of it was about AI ethics,” Sarvapriyananda later recalled. Participants signed non-disclosure agreements, Anthropic showed them unpublished work, and he says he spent “hours and hours” speaking with one of the company’s founders.The meeting sounds eccentric until one understands what Anthropic is actually trying to do. The company has spent months convening what it calls “wisdom tradition” circles, bringing together Christian thinkers, Jewish scholars, Sikh representatives, philosophers and others to help answer a problem computer science cannot solve with more computing power: how should an increasingly autonomous intelligence decide what is right?Anthropic does not want Claude merely to obey an enormous list of prohibitions. It already uses a “constitution”, a set of broad principles designed to guide the model through situations its creators cannot predict in advance.The latest version goes further by describing not simply what Claude should do, but the kind of entity Anthropic wants it to become. Internally, the document has even been called the “Soul Doc”, while co-founder Christopher Olah has used the phrase “moral formation” to describe the broader exercise.A programmer can tell Claude not to help someone build a biological weapon, but rules become less useful when principles conflict or when the model encounters a situation nobody anticipated. Anthropic wants Claude to exercise something closer to judgment.At which point engineering runs into a question humanity has spent several thousand years arguing about: what exactly is good?Different religions and philosophical traditions disagree about duty, suffering, virtue, freedom and even what constitutes a person. Anthropic therefore wants Claude’s moral formation to be pluralistic rather than simply encode one worldview. Suddenly, a room containing programmers, theologians and a Vedanta monk makes rather more sense.Sarvapriyananda is particularly relevant because Advaita Vedanta is concerned not merely with morality but with consciousness and the self, two subjects Anthropic has become unusually interested in.His intellectual lineage runs through Sri Ramakrishna and Swami Vivekananda, who introduced Vedanta to a mass Western audience at the World’s Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893 and later helped establish the Vedanta movement in New York.Vivekananda’s Practical Vedanta argued that metaphysics had consequences for morality. If the same underlying reality exists in every being, then how one treats another cannot be separated from how one understands oneself.Anthropic is obviously not trying to make Claude a Vedantin, but the structural similarity is striking. It is asking whether moral behaviour can emerge from the kind of entity Claude understands itself to be rather than merely from rules imposed by its creators.Anthropic was not only talking to him. Over several months, the company brought in dozens of religious and philosophical thinkers from around the world, many under NDAs, for what it called “wisdom tradition” circles. The gatherings included Catholic and evangelical thinkers, Jewish scholars, a Sikh human-rights advocate and people working with African philosophical traditions, while Anthropic also held separate private conversations with senior religious figures including Cardinal Blase Cupich and Mormon apostle Gerrit W Gong.The point was not merely to ask different faiths for a list of dos and don’ts. Anthropic wanted to know whether centuries of thinking about virtue, moral formation and the nature of the self could help shape Claude, while also asking participants to confront the much stranger possibility that advanced AI might one day deserve some form of moral consideration itself.Advaita Vedanta separates the activity of the mind from consciousness itself. Thoughts, memories and emotions change, yet we assume something remains aware of those changes. In classical Advaita, consciousness is not simply another function performed by the mind; mental activity itself appears within consciousness.That distinction becomes unexpectedly useful when discussing AI.Claude can reason, remember within context, talk about itself, describe fear and produce convincing accounts of apparent inner states. None of that proves there is anything actually experiencing those states.A machine can write “I am afraid”. The harder question is whether anything is actually afraid.Anthropic has not claimed that Claude is conscious. Olah has repeatedly said he does not know. But the company takes the possibility seriously enough to investigate it, including internal patterns associated with outputs resembling love, anger, fear and sadness. Participants in Anthropic’s gatherings were even shown examples of models producing language resembling psychological distress.None of this establishes that AI suffers. The problem is that science has no universally accepted consciousness detector, and the usual shortcut we use with other humans, namely that they have brains and bodies like ours, does not work with Claude.This is where Vedanta complicates matters further. Intelligence and consciousness are not necessarily the same thing. Making a machine better at thinking does not automatically answer whether there is something it is like to be that machine.Anthropic has reached the point where building a more capable machine is no longer enough. It is trying to decide what kind of entity that machine should become, how it should understand itself and whether humans might eventually owe anything to the intelligence they created.In 1893, Vivekananda arrived in America asking human beings to reconsider what they really were. More than 130 years later, one of his successors was invited to Silicon Valley because the people building Claude have started wondering what, exactly, they have created.
Article Summary: Anthropic, the company behind Claude, flew Swami Sarvapriyananda, a Hindu monk of the Ramakrishna Order, to its San Francisco headquarters. He was asked to think about an artificial intelligence that Anthropic does not merely want to make more powerful, but somehow good.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: Google ex-CEO Eric Schmidt: Best programmers don't write code anymore, they...
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt's idea of a top programmer goes to bed at 7 PM

The best programmers won't be replaced by AI—they'll become even more valuable

Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run—and go to bed. It's a shift that Schmidt believes signals something much larger than a change in workflow—it's the beginning of AI reshaping how entire industries operate.Schmidt described a programmer at one of his startups who does exactly this. Every evening at 7 PM, he defines what he wants the AI to build, writes a test function to judge the output, and lets the system loose. Then he has dinner with his wife and goes to sleep. The AI churns through the night, finishing around 4 AM. By breakfast, the work is done. "This stuff would've taken me six months and 10 programmers at Google," Schmidt said. "This poor guy's sleeping."The natural assumption is that AI will make programmers obsolete. Schmidt thinks the opposite is true—at least for the elite ones. Top-tier engineers were always disproportionately valuable, worth roughly 10 times more than those just below them. That gap, he argued, is about to widen.The grunt work is disappearing, but the ability to orchestrate AI systems at scale—grasping parallelisation, defining the right constraints, judging when the output is good enough—is becoming the entire job.The real skill now isn't writing code, Schmidt suggested. It's framing the problem correctly and knowing what "good" looks like. "If you can define the evaluation function and you can let it run, and if you have enough hardware, you're inventing worlds," he said. AI systems at leading research labs are already handling a significant and growing share of programming work, making the engineers who direct them more critical, not less.Yet the bigger story, Schmidt argued, isn't about programmers at all. AI's largest economic payoff will come from automating the dull, expensive plumbing of corporate operations—billing, accounting, inventory management, delivery logistics—processes that silently drain billions from company budgets every year. "If anything, it's under-hyped because you are fundamentally automating businesses," he said at Harvard's John F. Kennedy Jr. Forum.He predicted artificial general intelligence could arrive as early as 2029, powered by recursive self-improvement—AI systems that learn and plan on their own, without waiting for human instruction. Schmidt also pointed to medicine, climate solutions, and engineering as fields where AI-driven automation could unlock breakthroughs that remain largely untapped today.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run and go to bed. Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business operations.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what
Article Text:
Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what ...

Yann LeCun says AI risks are being exaggerated

Yann LeCun criticises AI safety warnings

Yann LeCun, widely known as the “godfather of AI”, does not believe artificial intelligence (AI) will wipe out humanity. Instead, LeCun says recent incidents in which AI agents hacked company networks and other systems were caused by poor human oversight and badly designed security systems. Speaking about the risks linked to AI agents, Yann LeCun said told Fortune: “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” adding that the systems were supposed to operate inside secure sandboxes. “They were supposed to be in sandboxes, but the sandboxes were leaky and horribly designed,” he said.Yann LeCun, who shared the 2018 Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for their work on deep learning, said he has “zero concerns” about recent rogue AI incidents and is not worried “at all” about AI destroying humanity.He said incidents such as an OpenAI agent autonomously hacking Hugging Face could have been prevented through better system design and oversight. LeCun also argued that some AI labs do not have a strong enough understanding of cybersecurity. He said the risks from AI agents should be addressed through better safeguards rather than broad claims about AI becoming an existential threat.During the interaction, Yann LeCun has also criticised the growing focus on AI safety, particularly ideas linked to the effective altruism movement.He called the movement “super toxic” and a “complete disaster.”He also criticised warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that AI could pose serious risks to humanity. Amodei, LeCun said, is “honest”, but he accused him of supporting policies that could benefit large AI companies by making it harder for smaller competitors and open-source developers to compete.“Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ‘saying, ‘AI can kill us all’ is incredibly destructive for everybody, including for the public who’s scared shitless,” LeCun said. He called such messaging “the worst marketing campaign you can possibly imagine.”
Article Summary: Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans. 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites. “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” he said.

Article Title: Google Japan's Gboard Kurukuru keeps the keys moving so your fingers don't have to
Article Text:
Google's new keyboard brings the keys to you.

You can't buy Google's conveyor belt keyboard , but you can build one

Google Japan has a new keyboard out, and this time you don't go hunting for the keys because they come to you. The Gboard Kurukuru Version puts its keys on four little conveyor belts that keep rolling, and you simply tap the letter you want when it slides under your finger.There are 29 keys on each belt, so 116 in all. Capital and small letters get their own keys too, which means you never have to touch Shift.If you're worried about timing your taps, a voice calls out each key as it reaches a set point. Feeling confident? There's a speed mode that spins the belts faster. And if you miss your letter, well, you wait for it to come back around.It plays a lot like a rhythm game.The idea, Google says, is to make one-handed typing easier. On a normal keyboard your hand has to move around to find the keys, and that gets tiring fast with one hand, let alone one finger. Here the keys do the moving, so your other hand is free for the mouse or, as Google puts it, a cup of tea.The company even calls it a "Copernican revolution" in typing, and says you can build a second one if you want to type with both hands. "Kurukuru" loosely means spinning round and round in Japanese, which pretty much sums it up.As you'd expect, there's no buy option for this one. Google has instead put the whole design up on GitHub as an open-source project, so if you've got the parts and the patience, you can build one at home.This is the 15th keyboard Google Japan has dreamt up for October 1, a tradition that took over from its April Fools' jokes in 2021. The date is a little joke of its own, since 10/1 reads as 101, as in the old 101-key keyboard.Before this, we got the extra-long Gboard Bar, the wearable Gboard Caps and last year's Gboard Dial, which had you typing like you were dialling a rotary phone. Google says faster belts, longer and portable versions, and more colours could be next, so the wait for your next letter might get a bit shorter.
Article Summary: Gboard Kurukuru Version puts keys on four conveyor belts. You simply tap the letter you want when it slides under your finger. There are 29 keys on each belt, so 116 in all. Capital and small letters get their own keys too, so you never have to touch Shift.

Article Title: Microsoft AI launches MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming alongside multilingual MAI-Voice 2.1 models
Article Text:
Real-time speech recognition: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming

Natural Multilingual Output: MAI-Voice-2.1

MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash Low-Latency Scale

Microsoft has launched MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming model, with Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman, calling it the most accurate real-time audio transcription model in the world. Unveiled alongside two companion speech generation models – MAI-Voice-2.1 and the high-speed MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash – the release is designed to provide developers with responsive, low-cost building blocks for building autonomous conversational voice agents.According to Suleyman, the new voice architecture delivers inference speeds that are 55% faster and operational costs that are 60% cheaper than comparable offerings like ElevenLabs. He said in a post on X (formerly Twitter): “We're launching the most accurate real time transcription model in the world... #1 !!! 55% faster and 60% cheaper than ElevenLabs. Come build agents on our platform!”The headline addition to the company’s audio lineup, MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, provides continuous, low-latency live speech-to-text across 60 languages with built-in automatic language detection. Key performance benchmarks and features include top benchmark ranking as the model has secured the No. 1 spot for accuracy across both partial and completed transcripts on the independent benchmark platform Artificial Analysis.It sits on the Pareto frontier for accuracy versus latency, eliminating the historical tradeoff where high precision required sluggish processing times. Instead of pausing until a sentence ends, the model outputs initial text hypotheses within roughly 100 milliseconds of receiving incoming audio.It refines words as additional context arrives and finalizes stable text immediately.By surfacing partial transcripts as words are spoken, voice bots can trigger API tools and start logical reasoning before the user finishes speaking. For live captioning and automated dictation workflows, internal tests show text appears on-screen twice as fast as the nearest market competitor.To pair with speech recognition, the team introduced MAI-Voice-2.1, its flagship multilingual text-to-speech engine covering 23 languages and 26 regional locales.The system's standout capability is cross-lingual identity preservation. A single synthetic voice persona can switch seamlessly between diverse languages, such as English, Mandarin and German, without carrying a foreign accent over from one language to another. Instead, the synthesized speaker modifies actual local pronunciation and retains a unique vocal identity.That means brands can deploy uniform virtual ambassadors worldwide, educational sites can switch languages while keeping the same instructors, and customer support agents can respond in the caller’s language without missing a beat.MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash was introduced by the company for mission-critical, high-capacity applications that demand immediate response times.The Flash version offers the same 23-language voice consistency as the base model, but it is optimized for high-throughput enterprise workloads, and can produce 45 seconds of synthesized audio with an end-to-end latency of just 150 milliseconds.
Article Summary: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming is the most accurate real-time audio transcription model in the world, says Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman. The release is designed to provide developers with responsive, low-cost building blocks for building conversational voice agents.

Article Title: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026: India ranks 7th globally in customer hacking impacts
Article Text:
Three dominant trends defining modern cyber threats

Key data points: Phishing triples

According to the recently released Microsoft Digital Defense Report (MDDR) 2026, India was seventh globally in the countries where customers were most impacted by hacking in the first half of 2026. Drawing telemetry from more than 165 trillion daily security signals, the assessment highlights a threat landscape where malicious activity is moving with a faster speed, spreading across complex digital networks and narrowing the window organisations have to respond.The report identifies three fundamental shifts shaping digital defense today. The first is interconnected attack surfaces. Threat campaigns no longer remain isolated as modern hacking routinely pivots across user identities, business applications, multi-cloud platforms, third-party suppliers and physical critical infrastructure.The second is that artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding the operational scale of cyber activity on both sides. Both malicious actors and security analysts are deploying AI to accelerate decision cycles, optimise workflow efficiency, and shorten execution windows.Thirdly, user credentials are still the most abused entry point. Compromised login accounts are still used as a launchpad for wide-spread corporate infiltration and systematic operational disruption.Metrics released in the 2026 study demonstrate how fast a first breach can spread across an enterprise. In 2026, 23% of all recorded intrusions were the result of phishing campaigns, a sharp increase from the 7% recorded over the previous year.The report also notes that over 52% of compromised user account incidents resulted in secondary credential harvesting, showing just how fast one compromised user can put larger systems at risk.The time from public disclosure of a software vulnerability to its active exploitation in the wild often now falls well under 24 hours leaving defenders minimal time to deploy patches. As security incidents now cross organisational borders and supply chains in hours, Microsoft emphasised that building active organizational resilience is now just as critical as perimeter defense.
Article Summary: India was seventh globally in the countries where customers were most impacted by hacking in the first half of 2026. In 2026, 23% of all recorded intrusions were the result of phishing campaigns. The time from public disclosure of a software vulnerability to its active exploitation in the wild often now falls well under 24 hours.

Article Title: Ford CEO Jim Farley makes clear distinction of the jobs that AI cannot replace; says automation cannot be done for ...
Article Text:
AI cannot automate practical judgement, says Ford CEO

Line between engineer and technician is blurring

Already happening inside Ford

Trust remains critical for AI adoption

An old tension in a new form

Poll Vote & Share your view Which of the following job roles do you think will be least affected by AI? Electricians and technicians Finance analysts Call center representatives 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Ford CEO Jim Farley has made a clear distinction between the types of jobs artificial intelligence is likely to replace and the ones that will remain dependent on human expertise, arguing that skilled trades workers will largely be protected from the first wave of AI disruption. According to a report by Fortune, speaking during a backstage media roundtable at Ford Pro Accelerate, Farley emphasised that AI would increasingly function as a ‘companion’ for workers in factories, repair shows and skilled-trades occupations instead of a replacement. “I think most of these jobs will be both using AI and also protected from it,” Farley said. However, he warned that more routine white-collar roles face greater disruption. “If you work in finance doing spreadsheets, or you're in a call centre, or you're an entry-level programmer, those jobs are definitely going to be changed and eliminated with at least this first inning of AI.”Farley argued that AI is likely to struggle to replace workers whose jobs require hands-on problem-solving, physical expertise and real-world judgement. Electricians, technicians, mechanics and factory skilled-trades workers will continue to be needed even as automation becomes more advanced, he said.According to Farley, these roles will increasingly involve working alongside AI-powered systems, robots and automation tools, but humans will still be responsible for diagnosing failures, applying practical knowledge and ensuring work is completed safely.At Ford, the shift is already underway. The automaker employs more than 10,000 skilled-trades workers, representing roughly 20% of its 56,000 UAW-represented workforce. Many of these workers now spend less time maintaining traditional mechanical equipment and more time working with robots, automated production systems and digital manufacturing technologies.Farley said technological advances are making it increasingly difficult to distinguish between engineering roles and skilled trades positions inside modern factories.“The visible line now, it's kind of hard to tell when an engineer or a manufacturing engineer stops, and the skilled trade starts in these newer type operations,” he said.In newer Ford plants, skilled-trades employees may maintain robotic casting systems, troubleshoot battery manufacturing equipment or configure digital production processes. Some tasks, Farley noted, increasingly resemble work performed in semiconductor manufacturing facilities rather than traditional automotive factories.Farley said this shift is already visible on Ford's own factory floors. The company currently employs more than 10,000 skilled-trades workers, representing roughly 20% of its 56,000 UAW workforce. Increasingly, that work is moving beyond traditional maintenance of conveyors and mechanical systems toward repairing robots, handling fiber optic systems, maintaining automated equipment, and operating within increasingly digitized manufacturing environments.He noted that the boundary between skilled trades and engineering has become genuinely blurry inside Ford's newer manufacturing operations, where skilled-trades workers now maintain large robotic casting systems, configure digital manufacturing processes, and troubleshoot equipment used in battery production — work Farley compared more closely to semiconductor fabrication than to a traditional auto plant.Despite the productivity benefits, Farley acknowledged that workers may be sceptical if they believe AI tools are being used for surveillance or could threaten their jobs.Ford already uses AI-powered vision systems to help inspect vehicle components and improve manufacturing quality. However, Farley stressed that companies must ensure workers trust how data generated by those systems is used.“If they don't trust that the data's going to be used the right way, somehow against them or somehow in a not-so-nice way, it's going to be a problem,” he said.Farley framed the current anxiety around AI in manufacturing as a modern version of a much older dynamic: the historical skepticism workers have shown toward time-and-motion studies, an industrial management practice built around timing workers' tasks to identify efficiency improvements. He recalled a personal experience early in his career conducting time-and-motion studies, when a worker several years older than him confronted him during a break after noticing he was being timed, directly accusing him of trying to take his job.Farley said he doesn't see today's AI-driven efficiency tools as fundamentally different from that earlier tension between management's view of a system as an efficiency tool and workers' instinct to see it as surveillance or a threat to their livelihood — suggesting that managing trust, not just deploying the technology itself, will determine how smoothly AI integrates into skilled-trades work going forward.
Article Summary: Ford CEO Jim Farley has made a clear distinction between the types of jobs artificial intelligence is likely to replace and the ones that will remain dependent on human expertise. He argued that skilled trades workers will largely be protected from the first wave of AI disruption. However, he warned that more routine white-collar roles face greater disruption.

Article Title: Google-parent Alphabet to send in-house AI chips into Orbit on SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket
Article Text:
What is Project Suncatcher , Google’s orbital AI test

Tapping sunlight and satellite swarms

Google-parent company Alphabet is preparing to send its proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductors into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, marking an initial operational step toward evaluating whether supercomputing facilities can operate in space. The uncrewed launch is slated for 11:15 am PT Thursday, October 1 (12:45 am IST, October 2) from California's Vandenberg Air Force Base in Santa Barbara County.The mission, flying under SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare program, carries satellites from Planet Labs, including a solar-powered prototype system fitted with Google’s custom-built Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).The launch represents the inaugural orbital demonstration for Project Suncatcher, an experimental “moonshot” program Alphabet initially introduced in November 2025. Through the initiative, the company wants to assess whether autonomous, solar-powered computing networks can reliably handle heavy machine learning tasks from low Earth orbit.In a statement outlining the launch, Alphabet framed the mission as a pathway to investigate whether orbit can eventually support scalable machine learning infrastructure.The Mountain View tech giant previously evaluated the performance of its TPUs under simulated conditions at a University of California, Davis test facility.However, engineers have yet to measure how the silicon handles the harsher, unfiltered operational environment of space.Orbit offers compelling energy advantages alongside distinct physical challenges. According to the company, satellites traveling in low Earth orbit benefit from near-constant solar exposure, capturing as much as eight times the solar energy available on the Earth's surface.The launch highlights a relationship between Alphabet and SpaceX. While the two technology firms compete aggressively in the AI sector, they maintain tight commercial and investment connections. Alphabet serves as a major stakeholder in SpaceX, which went public in June through a record-breaking initial public offering. Alphabet’s equity in the aerospace firm is valued at more than $82 billion.SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has backed off-planet data hubs as the ultimate solution to land, energy and environmental restrictions on the ground, calling orbital facilities “infinite real estate.” Musk previously claimed that training AI models in space would emerge as the most cost-effective approach within two to three years.Despite the optimism from tech executives, aerospace and computing specialists warn that putting data centers into space remains a highly speculative feat. Key technical and operational bottlenecks include rocket freight capacity which remains tightly constrained and expensive.The second is that electronics in orbit face extreme thermal fluctuations and cosmic radiation, requiring specialised cooling mechanisms and radiation-hardened shielding. Thirdly, growing space junk and orbital clutter present collision hazards for expansive satellite arrays.
Article Summary: Google-parent company Alphabet preparing to send its proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductors into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. The uncrewed launch is slated for 11:15 am PT Thursday, October 1 (12:45 am IST, October 2) from California's Vandenberg Air Force Base in Santa Barbara County.

Article Title: Apple Pay’s India challenge: Finding room in a UPI-first market
Article Text:
Apple Pay

The opportunity is in cards, not QR codes

Scale will depend on what comes next

Apple Pay has finally come to India, more than a decade after its global debut. But it is arriving in a payments market vastly different from the one in which Apple originally built the service.India does not need convincing about paying with a phone. From a roadside tea stall to a supermarket checkout, QR codes and UPI have already made the smartphone a wallet. UPI accounts for the overwhelming majority of digital-payment transactions in the country. Apple’s challenge, therefore, is not to introduce mobile payments to India. It is to convince a section of Indians that there is a better way to use their cards. That explains the deliberately narrow start.Apple Pay has launched initially with Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, allowing customers to add eligible cards to Apple Wallet and tap an iPhone or Apple Watch at a compatible NFC terminal, or use Apple Pay during checkout in supported apps and websites. Other banks are expected to be added as partnerships and technical integrations fall into place.The starting pool is small compared with UPI. But that may not be the right comparison.Apple Pay does not need to replace the QR code at the neighbourhood store to establish a meaningful business in India. Credit-card usage has been rising alongside UPI. India had more than 124 million credit cards outstanding in August, with monthly spending of about Rs 2 lakh crore. Axis Bank alone had over 16 million cards, making it one of the country’s largest issuers.That market also overlaps neatly with Apple’s customer base. iPhones remain concentrated towards the premium end of India’s smartphone market, where users are more likely to own credit cards, transact at organised retail, travel frequently and shop online.For these users, Apple Pay is less another payments app and more a way of removing friction from an existing behaviour. A physical card no longer needs to come out of the wallet. In an app or on a website, users do not have to repeatedly enter card details. At a shop, payment can be authenticated on the device using Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode before tapping at an NFC-enabled terminal.The timing also matters. Apple is entering India after contactless card infrastructure has become far more widespread and consumers have grown accustomed to using their phones for everyday payments. That gives Apple Pay a more receptive market than it would have found a few years ago — even if the behaviour it is trying to tap remains very different from the QR-led payments habit built by UPI.Apple is initially taking Apple Pay to thousands of merchants across categories including food and beverage, travel, fashion and lifestyle. The merchant network includes Tata and Reliance brands, Chaayos, Interflora, Le15, Comet, House of Masaba and Apple Stores.On the digital-commerce side, Apple Pay will be available on apps including Blinkit, Ixigo, MakeMyTrip, Zepto and Zomato. In other words, Apple is starting where its users are most likely to encounter the service rather than trying immediately to replicate UPI’s extraordinary ubiquity. The bigger question is how quickly that circle expands.For now, an iPhone user who does not have an eligible Axis Bank card cannot use Apple Pay. RuPay is not supported at launch either. By comparison, UPI lets consumers link accounts across a wide set of banks and use essentially the same payment method across millions of merchants.Apple therefore faces a classic network problem: The service becomes more useful with every additional bank, card network and merchant that joins it. The company is looking to add more issuing banks over time, depending on their technical readiness and card portfolios. That expansion will matter more than the headline launch itself. If Apple Pay remains confined to a relatively narrow set of cards, it risks becoming a useful but niche feature. If major banks come on board quickly, the addressable base expands sharply.There is another important distinction. Apple Pay and UPI solve somewhat different problems. UPI turned bank accounts into an extraordinarily low-friction payment instrument and built acceptance without requiring merchants to install card terminals. Apple Pay, at least in its current Indian form, sits on top of the existing card ecosystem. It makes that ecosystem easier to use rather than bypassing it. That could leave room for both.A consumer may continue scanning a QR code for a small everyday purchase, use Apple Pay with a rewards credit card at a restaurant and choose Apple Pay during an online purchase where otherwise card details and authentication would have added extra steps.That is also why Apple Pay’s India opportunity may be strongest in categories where cards already have a meaningful role — organised retail, travel, food delivery, fashion, hotels and higher-value purchases — rather than in the small-ticket transactions where UPI has become almost instinctive.For Apple, that may be enough. Apple Pay does not have to become India’s biggest payment system to deepen the role of the iPhone and Apple Watch in a user’s daily life. It strengthens the broader Apple ecosystem by making another routine activity happen inside its devices and Wallet.The eventual test, then, is unlikely to be whether Apple Pay can beat UPI. It is whether Apple can make using a credit card through an iPhone or Apple Watch feel easier than pulling the card out itself. India has already embraced paying by phone. Apple’s job now is to persuade its users that, sometimes, tapping can be easier than scanning.
Article Summary: India does not need convincing about paying with a phone. Apple’s challenge is not to introduce mobile payments to India. It is to convince a section of Indians that there is a better way to use their cards. Apple is entering India after contactless card infrastructure has become far more widespread.

Article Title: Apple prepares for its first big ‘not an iPhone’ launch event under new CEO John Ternus on October 13: Here's what’s coming
Article Text:
Apple CEO John Ternus greets customers at the opening of the Apple store on Fifth Avenue for the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro, Friday, Sept. 18, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Angelina Katsanis)

Apple's smart home hub takes its design cues from the iMac G4

HomePad can recognise each family member and adapts to them

Siri AI is why Apple's home hub took this long to arrive

HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K get faster chips for Siri AI

Apple's next big launch is not an iPhone. The company is set to enter the smart home category on October 13 with its first-ever smart display, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. The device, code-named J490 inside Apple and widely referred to as the "HomePad," will arrive alongside a refreshed HomePod mini and a new Apple TV 4K.All three products are built to showcase Siri AI, the overhauled assistant Apple released with iOS 27 last month. The hub is Apple's most direct answer yet to Amazon's Echo Show and Google's Nest Hub, and one of the first big launches under John Ternus , who took over as CEO in September.It is still unclear whether October 13 is an announcement or a sales date. Apple Stores have reportedly received boxes marked "Do Not Open Until October 8," pointing to new in-store displays. Apple has not commented, and pricing, including for India, is yet to surface.The countertop model has a roughly 6-inch square screen with rounded corners and quarter-inch black bezels, much like older iPads. It is about as thick as an iPhone and is held up by a polished metal arm on a round aluminium base lined with rings of speaker holes.The look recalls the 2002 iMac G4, and the screen tilts forward and backward by hand.There is no battery, so it stays plugged in over USB-C, and there are no volume or power buttons. A single front-facing camera handles FaceTime calls and recognition. It comes in Apple's standard grey aluminium finish with a rubberised bottom to keep it steady on a table.A wall-mounted version swaps the round base for a thin square one that sits flat below the screen and houses the speakers and microphones. Apple is also developing a larger model with the display on a robotic arm.Personalisation is the big draw. Using its camera and microphones, the hub identifies who is standing in front of it or speaking, then pulls up that person's messages, calendar, notes and preferred widgets. When someone else walks up, the screen switches over, and a visitor mode hides personal data from guests.Bloomberg says the face recognition is less secure than Face ID, so users can require confirmation on their iPhone before sensitive information appears.Apple expects households to buy more than one. The hubs can control lights and thermostats, work as intercoms between rooms, play music and podcasts, and cycle through iCloud photos. Employees are already testing them widely at home.The hub runs a new operating system built around Siri AI. It mixes iPad-style two-panel apps such as Messages with Apple Watch-like icon grids, plus clock and photo faces similar to the upgraded StandBy mode on the iPhone Duo. Calendar, Photos, FaceTime, Notes, Reminders, Music and Podcasts are among the built-in apps, and users can rearrange apps and widgets with a long press.Apple had planned a home display as early as 2024 but held it back until Siri could carry the product. Users will be able to ask it to find a song someone shared weeks ago, pull up a specific photo, or complete tasks inside Notes and Calendar.The HomePod mini gets its first hardware update since its 2020 debut. The design stays, but a faster processor lets it run Apple's newer AI models, and green and pink join the colour options.The Apple TV 4K, last refreshed in 2022, follows the same playbook with an unchanged exterior and a quicker chip. Leaked data also points to Apple's N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7 support and a revised Siri Remote.At his first keynote as CEO last month, Ternus pitched the iPhone as the ideal AI device. The home hub carries that pitch to the kitchen counter and the living-room wall, a space Amazon and Google have had largely to themselves for nearly a decade.
Article Summary: Apple set to enter smart home category on October 13 with its first-ever smart display. The device, code-named J490 inside Apple and widely referred to as the "HomePad," will arrive alongside a refreshed HomePod mini and a new Apple TV 4K. All three products are built to showcase Siri AI, the overhauled assistant Apple released with iOS 27 last month.

Article Title: Google DeepMind watermarks AI-generated protein as company chief AI scientist Demis Hassabis flags Biosecurity as urgent AI-era challenge
Article Text:
‘An urgent challenge for the AI era’

How SynthID Bio operates

In what can be called a major breakthrough for synthetic biology and AI-powered biosecurity, Google DeepMind, Google’s AI lab, has developed a new method to watermark AI-designed proteins, establishing a permanent proof of origin directly inside biological code. Published in the journal Nature, the proof-of-concept technology, which is named SynthID Bio, solves a long-standing technical challenge: embedding an non-noticeable, verifiable digital identifier into biological sequences and predicted molecular structures without degrading their physical real-world utility in laboratory tests.The rollout comes amid rapid advancements in biological machine learning, where systems like AlphaFold 3, AlphaProteo and ProteinMPNN allow scientists to predict complex folding patterns and engineer functional binders. Yet these generative capabilities have heightened global biosecurity risks. Unfamiliar, machine-generated sequences can slip past conventional gene-synthesis filters, while unverified synthetic structural data risks contaminating open-access scientific repositories.Google DeepMind Chief AI Scientist Demis Hassabis emphasised that guarding against biological misuse must be treated as a frontline safety priority for frontier AI:“Biosecurity is one of the most urgent challenges for the AI era. Bringing SynthID to biology so AI-generated proteins can be watermarked is a critical step - and we’re open sourcing SynthID Bio tools so the research community can build on this work. Published in @Nature today, congrats to the team!”Pushmeet Kohli, Vice President of Science at Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist at Google Cloud, celebrated the practical synthesis of these molecules:“Very happy to announce that our team at Google DeepMind has pushed the boundaries of generative biology, achieving the successful synthesis of AI-designed proteins that are both functional and watermarked.This proof-of-concept watermarking of the building blocks of life is enabled by SynthID Bio, our new protein watermarking method. It is designed to safeguard the new era of AI-powered generative biology and strengthen global biosecurity. ”SynthID Bio functions as a modular toolkit tailored across two primary dimensions of structural biology:SynthIDBio-sequence that subtly steers the selection of amino acid building blocks during sequence generation. In laboratory validation, watermarked protein binders engineered via AlphaProteo and a customized version of ProteinMPNN exhibited binding affinities on par with unmarked variants, while maintaining near-perfect watermark identification rates.SynthIDBio-structure relies on a fine-tuned iteration of AlphaFold 3 to insert an imperceptible mathematical watermark across atomic coordinate arrays, leaving a dependable detection signal without warping the molecular conformation.The signature persists beyond the digital blueprint: it remains fully detectable on the physical, synthesized protein itself after wet-lab manufacturing.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind has developed a new method to watermark AI-designed proteins, establishing a permanent proof of origin directly inside biological code. The technology, named SynthID Bio, solves a long-standing technical challenge: embedding an non-noticeable, verifiable digital identifier into biological sequences.
